clue.text: Scottish scene of Alfred's episode with the cakes?

parts.note: a bannock is a flat Scottish oatcake
King Alfred is said to have let a peasant woman's cakes burn

explanation.surface: A question about where in Scotland King Alfred famously spoiled the baking.
explanation.walkthrough: Bannockburn is the 1314 battle site in Scotland; read as two words it describes the legend of Alfred burning the cakes, though Alfred was English.
explanation.definitionFit: Bannockburn is a Scottish battlefield, a famous scene of Robert the Bruce's victory.

clue.text: Town in Lancaster not open — turn about

parts.note: Burt Lancaster was a Hollywood film star

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of these words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a town in Lancaster is closed and should turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NOT OPEN TURN into ONUPONTRENT. Burton upon Trent is an English brewing town in Staffordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Burton upon Trent is an English market town, famous for brewing beer.

clue.text: One in books group

indicators.note: in places the word one inside the abbreviation for the books

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: One person's name appears in a book club's records.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine, especially nine musicians.

clue.text: A swimmer, like a clodhopper crossing the river

indicators.note: crossing has the clumsy word stretched across the river's letter

parts.note: a clodhopper is a clumsy oaf, so oafish

explanation.surface: A clumsy swimmer floundering across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The oarfish is a very long ribbon-like sea fish, so a swimmer.

clue.text: She's a stinker, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of the word might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A rude remark that some woman smells bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirsten is a woman's first name, so a she.

clue.text: America ending negotiation without the bottom line

indicators.note: negotiation treats the letters as something to be worked over and rearranged

parts.note: US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: The USA walking away from talks before a deal is finalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiation' rearranges US plus ENDING; the bottom line of a document is where it is signed.
explanation.definitionFit: A document lacking its signature line filled in is not signed by anyone.

clue.text: County said to be tying with another lacking opening point

indicators.note: said to be means the word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: tying a cord is knotting it

indicators.note: lacking means a letter is left out of the other county

parts.note: Hampshire is another English county

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the word point

explanation.surface: A county is reported to be level with a rival which cannot quite score.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOTTING spoken sounds like NOTTING; Hampshire loses P, the opening of 'point', to give HAMSHIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottinghamshire is an English county in the East Midlands.

clue.text: Destroy species Thomas disposed of

indicators.note: disposed of suggests the letters have been set out again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Thomas has got rid of several species of wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to break it into fragments completely.

clue.text: New greatness of service catering establishment

definitions.text: New greatness of service catering establishment

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the word are formed afresh in another order

parts.note: a mess is where members of the armed forces eat

explanation.surface: A grand new military canteen is opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges GREATNESS into SERGEANTS; the whole clue loosely describes the dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeants' mess is the dining and social club for senior NCOs in the forces.

clue.text: Ancient stopper

parts.note: Coleridge's old sailor famously stops one of three wedding guests to tell his tale

explanation.definitionFit: In Coleridge's poem the ancient seafarer 'stoppeth one of three' to tell his story.

clue.text: Girl, an abstainer, takes drug as a favour

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
TT stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A teetotal girl agrees to take drugs to oblige someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon badge or rosette worn as a token of support.

clue.text: Happy, Grumpy, Bashful, Sleepy, Sneezy, Doc …

definitions.text: Happy, Grumpy, Bashful, Sleepy, Sneezy, Doc …

parts.words: Happy, Grumpy, Bashful, Sleepy, Sneezy, Doc …
parts.note: six of the seven dwarfs: the roll is one name missing, and its members are small

explanation.definitionFit: Six of the seven dwarfs named, so the roll is incomplete and its members are little people.

clue.text: One wearing a medal at work

indicators.note: the medal wraps around the numeral as clothes surround the wearer

parts.note: gong is slang for a medal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sporting a medal while on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is working is going, in operation.

clue.text: Trip to ancient site

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An excursion to see some ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey or excursion, a trip.

clue.text: Plant hunger — a bit unusual!

indicators.note: unusual signals that these letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A plant's appetite is rather odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunbergia is a genus of climbing plants such as black-eyed Susan.

clue.text: A small number entertained by a priest find it therapeutic

indicators.note: entertained by puts the number inside as a guest held by a host

parts.note: a curate is an assistant priest
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A few people visited by a clergyman feel better for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something curative heals, so it is therapeutic.

clue.text: For amusement, take time in amateur handicraft in depth

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
fun is amusement

indicators.note: take has the handicraft word holding the letter for time

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself home handiwork

explanation.surface: Amusing oneself with time spent on home crafts in great detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Profundity is deepness of thought or meaning, depth.

clue.text: Her grace may be celebrated

parts.note: Her Grace is the form of address for a noblewoman of the highest rank below royalty

explanation.definitionFit: A woman of ducal rank is styled Her Grace and is often a famed society figure.

clue.text: Where Clement settled in North Africa

definitions.text: Where Clement settled in North Africa

indicators.note: settled suggests the letters have come to rest in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man named Clement makes his home in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tlemcen is a city in north-western Algeria, so a place in North Africa.

clue.text: Last resort of 9

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means the letters are sorted again

explanation.surface: A seaside holiday spot is the final stop for a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 9 across, a sailor; an old salt is a seasoned seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is slang for a sailor, the same as a mariner.

clue.text: Bonus derived from illegal sex traffic

indicators.note: derived from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone makes extra money from the criminal sex trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something added on top, a bonus.

clue.text: Fashion some change into out East

indicators.note: into signals the letters are rearranged into the answer, and out signals the letter is left over

explanation.surface: Advice to adopt some new style when going out in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: SOME CHANGE has ten letters: drop one E and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheongsam is a high-necked Chinese dress, a style of fashion.

clue.text: Cheese gives rise to stink and prohibition

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: BO is body odour, a stink
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A smelly cheese causes a stench and gets itself banned.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is an important person, as is a nabob, a rich and powerful man.

clue.text: Solitary before getting widow's contribution

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
the widow's mite is the small coin given in Jesus's parable

explanation.surface: A lonely person earlier received a small sum from a widow.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, someone who lives in solitude.

clue.text: They are said to control taxes

definitions.text: They are said to control taxes

parts.words: They are said to control taxes
parts.note: taxes spoken sounds like taxis, the vehicles these drivers steer

explanation.definitionFit: Cab drivers steer taxis, which sound like taxes when spoken.

clue.text: A belt administered without cause is capitally offensive

indicators.note: without means outside, so the reworked letters surround the cause
administered suggests the letters are dealt out in a new order

parts.note: a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: A beating given for no reason deserves the harshest punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'administered' turns A BELT into TABLE, which goes around REASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason was punishable by death, so a treasonable act was a capital offence.
